Q1.answer: Peskas is connected to a comprehensive ecosystem of tools, datasets, research outputs, geographic locations, and partner organizations. Within its own initiative, Peskas comprises several R packages (peskas.timor.portal, peskas.timor.pipeline), software components (Peskas Data Ingestion & Analytics Pipeline, Peskas Automated Validation Engine, Peskas Web Dashboard, Peskas Tracks App, PeskAAS), validated trip datasets from Kenya, Mozambique, and Zanzibar, and documentation (monitoring system slides, timeline). It produces or shares data with multiple research outputs, including the Nature Food 2026 paper on fishery nutrient profiles for Timor-Leste and a Kenya-based digital feedback study. Peskas references or is referenced by shared concepts and partners: WorldFish (its parent organization), Fish & Aquatic-Food Nutrition, Small-Scale Fisheries, and geographic regions including Timor-Leste (origin), Zanzibar, Kenya, Mozambique, Tanzania, and Malawi. It also references external tools and frameworks like KoboToolbox, FishBase, the Nairobi Convention, ProFishBlue, and the Asia-Africa BlueTech Superhighway (AABS). The WIOMSA Data Harmonization Presentation cites Peskas as a case study. Peskas is led by Alexander Tilley and shares data with Beach Management Units (BMUs) in Kenya. It is conceptually related to the COASTS platform and functional requirements for electronic data collection tools.

Q2.answer: Peskas relates to the WIO SSF Data Harmonization Initiative through multiple substantive technical and conceptual connections documented in the WIO data harmonization work. Peskas is presented as a case study and exemplar within the data harmonization initiative's October 2025 WIOMSA presentation. Specifically: (1) Peskas is referenced as a digital SSF monitoring system exemplar that demonstrates functional requirements for electronic data collection; (2) Peskas uses KoboToolbox for data ingestion of fishing trip information, which is a tool documented within the data harmonization work; (3) Peskas exports and shares data via Dataverse, another platform referenced in the data harmonization initiative; (4) Peskas employs FishBase for data mining as part of its analytical approach, also referenced in the harmonization work; and (5) Peskas is compared alongside COASTS (the Small Scale Fisheries Analysis Platform) as an example of digital tools in the same problem space. Both initiatives reference the same substantive domains: Small-Scale Fisheries monitoring, WorldFish as a shared stakeholder organization, and alignment with the Nairobi Convention. The relationship is documented primarily through the WIOMSA Data Harmonization Presentation (Oct 2025), which uses Peskas as a case study to illustrate how existing digital monitoring systems can inform and exemplify the data harmonization initiative's standards and requirements.
